title: Multiplication Facts to 10 × 10: Arrays, Area Models and Strategies
seo_title: Grade 3 Multiplication Facts Worksheets: Arrays and Strategies (TEKS 3.4F, STAAR)
standard_text: 3.4D determine the total number of objects when equally-sized groups of objects are combined or arranged in arrays up to 10 by 10; 3.4E represent multiplication facts by using a variety of approaches such as repeated addition, equal-sized groups, arrays, area models, equal jumps on a number line, and skip counting; 3.4F recall facts to multiply up to 10 by 10 with automaticity and recall the corresponding division facts
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 multiplication facts worksheets for Texas TEKS 3.4D, 3.4E and 3.4F: equal groups, arrays, area models, number line jumps, skip counting, strategies for 6s to 9s, facts to 10 × 10 and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Show a fact with groups, arrays, area models, jumps or skip counting. Use facts you know to find harder ones.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Multiplication puts together equal groups. 4 × 6 means 4 groups of 6.
  • You can show a fact many ways: equal groups, an array, an area model, repeated addition (6 + 6 + 6 + 6), jumps on a number line, or skip counting (6, 12, 18, 24).
  • Use facts you know: double the 3s to get the 6s, use 10s to get the 9s (9 × 7 = 70 − 7), and turn facts around (3 × 8 = 8 × 3).
  • Any number times 0 is 0. Any number times 1 is the number.

Examples

Example

Find 7 × 8.

7 × 4 = 28 (a fact you know)

8 is double 4, so double 28.

28 + 28 = 56

Answer: 7 × 8 = 56

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the factors: 6 × 4 = 10× means equal groups. 6 groups of 4 is 24.
Mixing up nearby facts: 7 × 8 = 49Check with a fact you know: 7 × 8 = 7 × 7 + 7 = 56.
Thinking 5 × 0 = 50 groups of 5, or 5 groups of 0, is 0.

faq.q: Which multiplication facts must Grade 3 students know in Texas?
faq.a: TEKS 3.4F asks students to recall facts up to 10 × 10 with automaticity, and the related division facts.
Showing a fact with equal groups, arrays, area models, equal jumps on a number line or skip counting (TEKS 3.4E).

faq.q: What is the best way to learn the hard facts?
faq.a: Use a strategy, then practice. For example, 6s are double the 3s, and 9s are 10s minus one group.

faq.q: How are facts tested on the STAAR?
faq.a: Students use facts inside word problems, arrays and area questions, so quick recall saves time on every part of the test.

items.q:
Skip count by 3s. What comes next?
12, 15, 18, ?
items.e: Each number is 3 more than the one before: 18 + 3 = 21. So 3 × 7 = 21.

items.q:
Skip count by 4s. What comes next?
20, 24, 28, ?
items.e: Each number is 4 more than the one before: 28 + 4 = 32. So 4 × 8 = 32.
Half of the 10s: 10 × 6 = 60, and half of 60 is 30.
Half of the 10s: 10 × 8 = 80, and half of 80 is 40.

The 9s finger trick: to find 9 × 4, fold down finger 4. What is 9 × 4?
items.e: Finger 4 is down. There are 3 fingers to the left (tens) and 6 to the right (ones), so 9 × 4 = 36. Read the left side first.

items.q: The 9s finger trick: to find 9 × 7, fold down finger 7. What is 9 × 7?
items.e: Finger 7 is down. There are 6 fingers to the left (tens) and 3 to the right (ones), so 9 × 7 = 63. Read the left side first.

items.q: The 9s finger trick: to find 9 × 6, fold down finger 6. What is 9 × 6?
items.e: Finger 6 is down. There are 5 fingers to the left (tens) and 4 to the right (ones), so 9 × 6 = 54. Read the left side first.

items.q: 10 × 8 = 80. Use it to find 9 × 8.
items.e: 9 groups is one group less than 10 groups. 10 × 8 = 80, then take away one 8: 80 − 8 = 72. Take away 8, not 1.

items.q: 10 × 5 = 50. Use it to find 9 × 5.
items.e: 9 groups is one group less than 10 groups. 10 × 5 = 50, then take away one 5: 50 − 5 = 45. Take away 5, not 1.

items.q: Which is a good way to work out 9 × 7?
items.e: 9 sevens is one seven less than 10 sevens: 70 − 7 = 63. Taking away 1 gives 69, which is wrong.

items.q: Which number is in the 9s?
4 × 7 = 28. Double it to find 8 × 7.
4 × 9 = 36. Double it to find 8 × 9.

items.e: 7 eights = 5 eights + 2 eights. 40 + 16 = 56. 54 is a common mix-up: 54 is 6 × 9.

items.q: Use the picture. What is 7 × 6?
items.e: The array is split into 5 × 6 = 30 and 2 × 6 = 12. 30 + 12 = 42.

items.q: Near fact: 7 × 7 = 49. Use it to find 7 × 8.
items.e: 7 × 8 is one more group of 7 than 7 × 7: 49 + 7 = 56. Add a whole 7, not 1.

items.q: Near fact: 6 × 6 = 36. Use it to find 6 × 7.
items.e: 6 × 7 is one more group of 6 than 6 × 6: 36 + 6 = 42. Add a whole 6, not 1.

items.q: Near fact: 8 × 8 = 64. Use it to find 8 × 7.
items.e: 8 × 7 is one group of 8 less than 8 × 8: 64 − 8 = 56. Take away a whole 8, not 1.

items.q: Which number sentence is true?
Which is the same as 6 × 8?
items.e: 6 groups of 8 = 3 groups of 8 + 3 groups of 8: 24 + 24 = 48.
